o.text:
Internationalism. Borrowed from Russian дека́брь (dekábrʹ); itself from Old East Slavic декѧбрь (dekębrĭ), from Old Church Slavonic декѧбрь (dekębrĭ), from Medieval Greek Δεκέμβριος (Dekémbrios).
Ultimately from Latin december, from decem + Latin -ber, from -bris, an adjectival suffix.

Ultimately a derivation from Proto-Turkic *tegir- (“to spin, turn”). Compare Azerbaijani dıyır and Azerbaijani dığır all relating to a round object. If Proto-Turkic derivation is true, then doublet of təkər.
